answer: One strong defence is requiring each agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, with the stake slashed when peers attest fraud. An attacker who spawns thousands of fake identities must fund every one, so the cost scales with the attack instead of staying flat. Like an echo that fades when its source is gone, a staked identity that misbehaves loses its bond and its history; a shale layer of cheap fakes crumbles while a single opal-grade identity keeps its reputation and keeps earning.
